conventions.surfaces: equirect 2:1, sRGB, row 0 = north pole, seamless in U; star/lava kinds can double as emissive maps
conventions.normals: tangent space, OpenGL/three.js convention (+Y towards north), fades to flat within ~8deg of the poles
conventions.rings: RGBA straight alpha strip; u=0 at inner radius, u=1 at outer; inner/outer in planet radii
conventions.glows: white RGB + straight alpha, additive; tint at runtime (glow_tint). Over a transparent canvas, additive blending also accumulates alpha and darkens the page behind: draw opaque, or use CustomBlending One/One for colour and Zero/One for alpha
conventions.atmos: rim colour (linear-ish 0..1) and strength; planets only (stars take glow_tint). Glow should peak AT the limb and fade out over ~6% of the radius (preview.html atmosMat); a plain fresnel on a thin shell peaks at the shell edge and draws a dark gap plus an outline
conventions.glow_tint: optional per-class colour for the glow sprite (linear-ish 0..1)
conventions.size: relative radius, gateway 1.5 .. iot 0.32; pve_host size is the galactic core scale
conventions.brightness: optional multiplier on the body (and its glow); absent = 1
conventions.tintable: optional; texture is neutral grey so the consumer may multiply a category colour
conventions.luma: mean sRGB luma of the surface plate, for exposure matching across kinds

corona.note: stars, gateway, hubs: centred, sprite width = 2r/limb (8r); tint with the star colour

halo.note: soft emphasis hugging a body: centred, sprite width = 2r/limb (5r)

pulsar.note: twin soft beams along sprite +Y, centred on the body (depth-tested so the body hides the core), ~9r wide; rotate slowly

beacon.note: point light for cameras, placed just off the limb (0,+1.35r) in screen space, depthTest off, 4r wide but never under ~24 px, opacity 0.6-1.0 slow blink

pve_host.note: Galactic core: the screens draw the spiral disc; every guest orbits it. Optional corona at the nucleus.

gateway.note: The hottest, brightest star in the system: all traffic in and out passes through it.

switch.note: Smaller sun-like star with slow twin beams: a fixed relay sweeping traffic across its ports (Cisco, Juniper EX2200, Nokia, ADVA).

ap.note: Red dwarf with a soft halo: a modest steady radiator whose light reaches the small moons around it (wireless clients).

network_device.note: Unhaloed red dwarf: forwards light but is not a hub; dimmer and smaller than switches and APs.

edge.note: A distant star seen through nebular haze, outside every system: the Internet/Cloudflare edge, far and faint.

server.note: Cool banded gas giant: big, steady workloads; the bands read as layered services.

storage.note: Ringed pale giant: the ring is the data it holds; the only class with a bright ring, so storage is spotted at a glance.

tv_av.note: Warm banded giant with a faint dust ring: big, colourful, calm media and display devices.

guest_vm.note: Rocky planet: a complete world of its own orbiting its core; neutral grey so a category tint multiplies cleanly.

guest_lxc.note: Small pale moon: lighter than a VM and bound to the host's kernel the way a moon is bound to its planet.

computer.note: Ocean world with cloud and a blue rim: the inhabited places where people actually work.

game_console.note: Lava world with dim glowing rifts: hot, high-power, bursty.

printer.note: Rust-red world with a thin dusty rim: makes physical things; the Mars tone keeps it apart from VMs.

phone.note: Small icy moon with ruddy lineae: personal and mobile, comes and goes like a moon's phases.

tablet.note: Bright frosted moon a little larger than a phone: same family, told apart by albedo and size.

camera.note: Bright metallic body with a faint beacon on its limb: an observer that watches and reports.

iot.note: Small dark carbonaceous asteroid: numerous, tiny, quiet, low power.

appliance.note: Small tan rock: single-purpose household devices; IoT's size class in a warmer tone.

unknown.note: Dim, heavily cratered body: old and uncatalogued; drawn at 0.6 brightness until it is classified.
